argument.text: Fix tau>0 and real alpha,beta. If either phase is zero the definition of eta gives zero. Otherwise put hcov(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)), with s in [0,tau]. Then eta=tau^(-1)integral hcov(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The identity hcov(s)=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r))dr and the bound |exp(ix)-exp(iy)|<=|x-y| give |hcov(s)|<=tau*|alpha|, and more precisely |hcov(0)|+|hcov(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|. argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest magnitudes are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair has sum magnitude <=2N3. Thus the quotient is <=6/N3. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily and are included in these alternatives. These arguments prove the universal assertions with no remaining assumptions.

argument.text: Begin with finite support. Decompose each sequence into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, with shell norms X_(r,j). Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices, and relabel slots within this calculation so j1>=j2>=j3>=j4. For fixed values of the two smaller frequencies, the sum of the two large-frequency sequences constrained by the zero sum is <=X_(1,j1)X_(2,j2) by Cauchy–Schwarz (translated reflection preserves the ell2 norm). A shell has 2^(j+1) integer entries, so summing the two small sequences in ell1 gives <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r X_(r,jr). Dividing by Third>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

argument.text: Choose once eps as in F002; keep this fixed through the stage argument. Fix arbitrary periodic f,g and assume L1: f belongs to H^gamma and g belongs to H^agamma. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E004 with sigma_s=gamma, source g=f and source h=g. If gamma<1/2 its required second exponent is 1/2-gamma=agamma, and if gamma>1/2 it is 0=agamma. If gamma=1/2, use epsilon=eps, which is admissible by F002. The required second exponent is then eps, rather than agamma=1/8. Since eps<=1/8, F001 gives g in H^eps and ||g||_(H^eps)<=||g||_(H^(1/8)). In all cases F001 supplies the actual source memberships and converts the source inequality, leaving a factor sqrt(2*pi) in its constant. Thus ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma). At gamma=1/2 the constant may depend on the single fixed eps chosen solely from the two source statements; it is independent of f,g and all numerical data. Fix arbitrary real M0,tau,t, nonnegative integer n and periodic w. Assume L2: 0<tau<=1, t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], and w is time-independent, mean-zero, belongs to H^gamma and satisfies ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. In particular M0>=0. H002 and F001 give 0<gamma<=1 and w in Hsrc^gamma with ||w||_(Hsrc^gamma)<=sqrt(2*pi)*M0. In E003 set sigma_s=gamma, tau_s=tau, j=n, t_j=n*tau and g1=g2=w. For gamma=1/2 use epsilon=eps from F002, so beta0=-1/2-eps; otherwise use the source's prescribed beta0. The source integral is Stage_n(t;w): D005 identifies exp(s partial_x^3)=S_(-s) and exp(-s partial_x^3)=S_s, D016 identifies the integrand, and D021 has the same integral and factor 1/2. This equality holds on polynomials and for the distributional stage by extension; the source bounds provide its bounded extension in the norms used here. Apply E003 first with beta=agamma. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and agamma=1/2-gamma, giving agamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0, agamma<=1+gamma, and theta=(1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma). Its denominator is positive, and theta>=gamma since the numerator minus gamma times the denominator is (gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. For gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-eps<agamma=1/8<3/2, and theta=(11/8)/(2+eps). Since 0<eps<=1/8, theta>=11/17>1/2=gamma. For gamma>1/2, beta0=gamma-1<=0=agamma<=1+gamma and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma because gamma<=1. Thus each beta is allowed and each exponent denominator is positive. After F001 converts both sides, E003 yields ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^agamma)<=C_gamma*tau^theta*||w||_(H^gamma)^2. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta<=tau^gamma: (theta-gamma)log(tau)<=0. This gives the first pointwise bound by C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma. Apply E003 again to the same data with beta=1+gamma; this upper endpoint is allowed in all three cases and its time exponent is zero. Norm conversion gives ||Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2. Both constants are uniform in n,tau,t and support by E003; any dependence on eps is on the single fixed choice in S002. Taking one larger constant depending only on M0,gamma gives both asserted bounds. The stage has continuous representatives in these norms: the E003 endpoint formula, boundedness of Dinv from H^gamma to H^(1+gamma), strong continuity of the Airy multipliers, and continuity of multiplication on H^(1+gamma) give this. For completeness, the inverse-derivative bound follows from (1+k^2)/k^2<=2 on nonzero modes. Strong continuity follows by finite Fourier truncation and uniformly small square-summable tails. For r=1+gamma>1/2, multiplication is bounded on H^r by the weighted convolution inequality <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r), the ell^1-ell^2 convolution bound, and Cauchy-Schwarz with sum_k<k>^(-2*r)<infinity. These establish the endpoint formula's continuity and the polynomial extension; H^(1+gamma) embeds in H^agamma by F001. The pointwise estimates with a common constant therefore bound both time suprema on the step as specified by D004. Discharge L2 and universally quantify the arbitrary stage data. Together with S002 this proves exactly N007; the auxiliary eps does not occur in its assertion.

argument.text: H002 supplies the range 0<gamma<=1 and the guard for agamma. Fix smooth data, an exact twisted flow with H^gamma bound M0, and a step with delta_n<=1. Put w=v(t_n), so N009–N010 apply. In the first integral of rho_n, integrate Bop_t(Y_n,z_n) by N005's normal form, keeping both endpoints. The asymmetric Jop estimate and sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C tau q_n bound the endpoint terms by C tau q_n. The term integral Jop_t(Y_n',z_n) is <=tau*C q_n by the Dinv Y_n' bound and ||z_n||_2<=C. Since z_n'=(1/2)Bop_t(f_n,f_n), the other term is (1/2)Cop(f_n,f_n,Y_n). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y_n: its first term is <=C tau q_n because f_n is constant with bounded Xnorm and ||Y_n||_X<=C q_n; its second term is <=C tau q_n by the small H^(-pstar) norm of Y_n. Thus the first integral of rho_n is <=C tau q_n, uniformly at every partial-step endpoint.

produces.statement: For every partial endpoint of the step, ||integral Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)dt||_2<=C tau q_n.

argument.text: For integral Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n), the same normal form gives endpoint terms <=C tau q_n^2 and derivative terms <=tau*C q_n^2 using the asymmetric Jop estimate, Dinv Y_n and Dinv Y_n', and ||Y_n||_2<=C q_n. Since q_n<=2 this is <=C tau q_n. The affine W_n term is <=||W_n||_2<=C tau q_n by N009. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C tau q_n. By N008, Rres'=-Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)-(1/2)Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n)-W_n/tau; N005's Bop negative-norm bound, N009–N010 and q_n<=2 give ||Rres'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C q_n.

produces.statement: On a step with delta_n<=1, sup||rho_n||_2<=C tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C q_n.

argument.text: Now fix any interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, and temporarily assume L1: E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps, each beginning within I, with delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I because N008 gives V(t_n)=v^n. Sum F002 over complete steps and the final partial step to obtain sup||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). Differentiating the exact twist gives v'=(1/2)Bop_t(v,v); subtract N008 to obtain e'=Bop_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 bounds its negative norm by C E_I+C(tau^gamma+E_I), proving ||e||_X<=C(tau^gamma+E_I). The exact L2 bound gives ||v||_X<=C; then V=v-e gives ||V||_X<=C, since tau^gamma<=1 and E_I<=1. Discharge L1, retain its antecedent, and quantify over all intervals and flows.

argument.text: H002 supplies the range 0<gamma<=1 and the guard for agamma. Fix the objects and assume L1: E_I<=1. From the exact twist equation and N008, e'=Bop_t(e,g)-Rres', with g=v-e/2; integration from a gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). The low frequencies satisfy ||P_leq(N)Bop_t(e,g)||_2<=C N^2||e||_2||g||_2: first use N005 on Dinv Pnz[(S_t e)(S_t g)], then multiply the remaining two Fourier derivatives by at most N^2. The group is unitary and ||g||_2<=C by N011. Integration over h gives sup||P_leq(N)F_I||_2<=C N^2 h E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact error identity holds and sup_I||P_leq(N)F_I||_2<=C N^2 h E_I.

argument.text: N005 applied to F_I retains both endpoints: F_I(t)=(1/3)[Jop_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)-(1/3)integral_a^t[Jop_s(e',g)+Jop_s(e,g')]ds. Since v'=(1/2)Bop(v,v), e'=Bop(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)Bop(v,v)-(1/2)Bop(e,g)+(1/2)Rres', symmetry of Jop and its Bop-to-Cop identity yield exactly F_I(t)=(1/3)[Jop_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Cop_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Cop_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t Jop_s(Rres',V)ds. Indeed the first cubic combination is Cop(e,g,g)-(1/2)Cop(e,g,e)=Cop(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V; the forcing is -Jop(Rres',g)+(1/2)Jop(e,Rres')=-Jop(Rres',V). After P_gt(N), both endpoints are <=C N^(-1) E_I by the H^1 Jop estimate, including the endpoint at a even when e(a)!=0. Apply the identity stepwise and telescope internal endpoints when necessary.

produces.statement: Under L1, for all t in I, F_I(t)=(1/3)[Jop_s(e,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)-(1/3)Cop_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Cop_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t Jop_s(Rres',V)ds, where V and Rres are D023 components. The P_gt(N) projection of the sum of the two endpoint terms has norm <=C N^(-1) E_I.

argument.text: For any three permitted inputs, put Low=P_leq(N/3) and High equal to its complementary Fourier projection. The expression Cop(f1,f2,f3)-Cop(Low f1,Low f2,Low f3) equals Cop(High f1,f2,f3)+Cop(Low f1,High f2,f3)+Cop(Low f1,Low f2,High f3). The all-low output has no frequencies above N, since each Fourier product has sum of its input frequencies and neither the group nor inverse derivative changes support. Projections contract Xnorm. For each designated high input, ||High fj||_(H^(-pstar))<=C N^(-pstar)||fj||_2 by its Fourier support. N006 with the negative norm on that slot therefore gives ||P_gt(N)Cop_[a,t](f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C h product||fj||_X(I)+C N^(-pstar) product||fj||_(L^infinity(I;L2)). For the two cubic terms of F002, N011 bounds the Xnorm of e by C(tau^gamma+E_I), all other Xnorms by C, and their L2 products by C E_I. Thus these terms total <=C h tau^gamma+C(h+N^(-pstar))E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1 the two high-output cubic terms in the normal-form formula total at most C h tau^gamma+C(h+N^(-pstar))E_I.

argument.text: It remains to bound the forcing integral in F002 using the actual residual. On each intersected step N008 rewrites Jop_s(Rres',V) as -Jop_s(Bop_s(Y_n,z_n),V)-(1/2)Jop_s(Bop_s(Y_n,Y_n),V)-tau^(-1)Jop_s(W_n,V). The first two integrals are -Cop(Y_n,z_n,V) and -(1/2)Cop(Y_n,Y_n,V) on the relevant subinterval. N009–N010 give ||z_n||_X<=C, ||Y_n||_X<=C q_n and sup||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C tau q_n. N011 gives ||V||_X<=C even on the final partial subinterval. Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y_n: each term is <=C tau q_n, using q_n<=2 for the term with two Y_n. The W_n integral is <=tau^(-1)*tau*C||W_n||_2 sup||V||_2<=C tau q_n by N005 and N009. Every intersected step starts inside I, so q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I; there are <=h/tau+1 such steps. Summing gives C(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I), also for a partial final step.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||integral_a^t Jop_s(Rres',V)ds||_2<=C(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I) for all t in I.

argument.text: Combine F002–F004 to get sup||P_gt(N)F_I||_2<=C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Use F001 and N011's bound on Rres(t)-Rres(a) in the error identity. Splitting into low and high outputs and absorbing fixed coefficients in C yields E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C(h+tau)tau^gamma+C(N^2 h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))E_I. Discharge L1 and quantify over I,N and the conditional smooth flows; no constant depends on the restart location or Fourier support.

locals.declaration: Take Mbound=1+A(T,gamma,R) from N001.
Take a common constant C_Mbound>=1 in N012 at flow bound Mbound, enlarging the positive supplied constant if necessary.
Define Ncut=max(2,8*C_Mbound). Since pstar>1 and Ncut>=2, C_Mbound*(Ncut^(-1)+Ncut^(-pstar))<=2*C_Mbound/Ncut<=1/4.
Define deltaBlock=min(1,1/(4*C_Mbound*(Ncut^2+3))).
Define Cprime_Mbound=3*C_Mbound.
Set Kblocks=ceiling(2*T/deltaBlock)+1.
Define Csmooth=1+(2^Kblocks-1)*Cprime_Mbound*deltaBlock.
Define tau0=min(1,deltaBlock/2,(1/(4*Csmooth))^(1/gamma)). H002 ensures the positive exponent is defined and Csmooth*tau0^gamma<=1/4.

argument.text: By H001–H003 and N001 take the common exact-flow bound Mbound=1+A(T,gamma,R). Take one constant C_Mbound>=1 in N012, valid for every smooth datum in the ball. Define Ncut=max(2,8*C_Mbound); since pstar=23/14>1, C_Mbound*(Ncut^(-1)+Ncut^(-pstar))<=2*C_Mbound/Ncut<=1/4. Define deltaBlock=min(1,1/(4*C_Mbound*(Ncut^2+3))) and Cprime_Mbound=3*C_Mbound. Restrict tau<=deltaBlock/2. For a grid-start interval of length h<=deltaBlock, C_Mbound*(Ncut^2*h+h+tau)<=C_Mbound*deltaBlock*(Ncut^2+3)<=1/4. Together with the frequency tail, the coefficient multiplying E_I in N012 is <=1/2. Absorbing it and using h+tau<=3*deltaBlock/2 gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+Cprime_Mbound*deltaBlock*tau^gamma whenever E_I<=1. The estimate includes h=0 directly.

produces.statement: For all smooth data in the ball and tau<=deltaBlock/2, every grid-start interval of length <=deltaBlock with E_I<=1 satisfies E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+Cprime_Mbound deltaBlock tau^gamma.

argument.text: Partition the grid into successive blocks of floor(deltaBlock/tau) steps and a possible shorter final block. Since tau<=deltaBlock/2, each full block has length between deltaBlock/2 and deltaBlock; the number of blocks is at most Kblocks=ceiling(2*T/deltaBlock)+1. Starting with e(0)=0, F001 iterates the scalar inequality E_j<=2 E_(j-1)+Cprime_Mbound*deltaBlock*tau^gamma. Finite induction gives E_j<=(2^j-1)Cprime_Mbound*deltaBlock*tau^gamma; thus sup||e||_2<=Csmooth*tau^gamma while the bootstrap holds, for a Csmooth independent of datum and timestep. For a stopping time inside a step apply F001 to the truncated final block; its proof allows that endpoint.

produces.statement: Until any bootstrap stopping time, sup||e||_2<=Csmooth tau^gamma, with Csmooth depending only on T,gamma,R.

argument.text: Define tau0=min(1,deltaBlock/2,(1/(4*Csmooth))^(1/gamma)). H002 gives gamma>0 and Csmooth>=1, so tau0>0 and Csmooth*tau0^gamma<=1/4<1/2. N001 provides the smooth exact flow and N008 provides continuous piecewise smooth V, hence e is continuous with e(0)=0. If ||e||_2 first reached one, at that first time all preceding step starts have delta_n<=1 and every block lies in the bootstrap region. F002 at that time would give ||e||_2<=Csmooth*tau^gamma<=1/4, a contradiction. No such time exists, and the uniform interpolation estimate holds throughout [0,T]. Only the initial H^gamma ball enters the constants.

produces.statement: There is tau0(T,gamma,R)>0 such that all smooth data in the ball satisfy sup_[0,T]||e||_2<=Csmooth tau^gamma for tau<=tau0.

argument.text: By N008 V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)u^n. Since S_t is unitary, ||e(t_n)||_2=||u(t_n)-u^n||_2. Thus F003 gives the grid estimate as well. The choices used only T,gamma,R through Mbound and the support-independent constant in N012. Quantifying over all smooth data and positive integer L proves the asserted smooth-data result with constants uniform over the whole smooth initial-data ball.

Fix arbitrary positive integer Lsteps; set tau=T/Lsteps and assume tau<=tau0 from N013.
Define u0m=P_leq(m)u0, m a positive integer.
Take the exact solution for u0 supplied by N001.
For each u0m take its smooth exact solution supplied by N001.
Use the uniform positive error constant C provided by N013, independent of datum and step size.
Use the positive uniform threshold tau0 provided by N013.
Set tau=T/Lsteps with tau<=tau0, as stipulated for the permitted integer Lsteps.

argument.text: H001–H003 give the target parameter ranges. Take C,tau0 from N013, which were chosen before fixing the datum or the step size. Assume L1: u0 is real mean-zero in H^gamma with norm <=R, and Lsteps is an arbitrary positive integer with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau0. Define u0m=P_leq(m)u0. Fourier truncation preserves reality and zero mean, gives ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and u0m->u0 in H^gamma and L2 because the tails of the defining positive square sum tend to zero. N001 supplies their smooth exact solutions and the unique limiting solution, with a common bound depending only on T,gamma,R. Its L2 Lipschitz estimate at B=2R gives sup_[0,T]||uapprox_m-uexact||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0m-u0||_2->0.

produces.statement: Under L1, the Fourier polynomial data stay in the same H^gamma ball and their exact flows converge uniformly in time in L2 to uexact.

argument.text: For this fixed tau>0, N005 proves continuity of Psi_tau on mean-zero L2 and preservation of real mean-zero functions. Induction over the finite number Lsteps of updates therefore gives u_m^n->u^n in L2 for each n=0,...,Lsteps, starting from u0m->u0. In particular the unmodified scheme is defined for u0 itself; no Fourier cutoff is introduced. All coefficients, including tau^(-1), remain finite in this fixed-timestep limit. N013 applies to every smooth u0m with precisely the same C,tau0. At each grid point combine convergence of the exact and numerical terms; by continuity of the norm its limit satisfies ||uexact(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The maximum over the finite set of Lsteps+1 points has the same bound (equivalently finite maxima commute with these limits).

produces.statement: Under L1 the full grid error for u0 and this arbitrary permitted Lsteps is <=C tau^gamma, with C,tau0 independent of u0 and Lsteps.

argument.text: Discharge L1, retaining every real, mean-zero, H^gamma and radius condition in the universal assertion. Quantify over u0 and Lsteps, renaming Lsteps to L. The constants remain the uniform constants already fixed in S001, independent of approximation support, datum and timestep. D001–D012 are exactly the selected domain, normalized norms, solution convention and fixed scheme; the final bound is therefore the complete selected Theorem 1.
